title: Newsletter: April to June 2025
summary: Training for pastors in Auki, a board visit, a sewing course, a container of donations and a busy season of bookings.
body:
Time flies when you are seeing God's work unfold. As we start a new quarter, we are glad to share the workshops, ministries and activities at the SWIM base. All glory to the Almighty for guiding our mission.

New security officer: we welcome Mr Mattew Tarai, from West 'Are'are in Malaita Province. He and his wife Hellen Hikimae Tarai have six children and three grandchildren. "I have been staying at the Plywood community and have seen the support that SWIM has done for us. I look forward to working to keep the SWIM base safe."

Auki leadership training: from 1 to 3 April, 20 pastors and leaders from SSEC, AOG, Anglican and COC churches met for worship, learning and fellowship. They thanked SWIM and Pastor Michael Light for the biblical training, resources and meals.

Board visit: SWIM board members Mike Vos and Daniel van Rensburg made an official visit. They interviewed staff, inspected the facilities, visited Bethesda Disability Care Centre, and finished at Rove Correctional Centre, where they saw the effect of the Crossroads ministry.

Sewing team: SWIM's 5-day sewing course ended with celebration. We are grateful to Jan, Ingeborg, Ella, Lois, Jola and Rose.

Container arrival: after weeks of preparation and paperwork, a container arrived safely at the base. Thanks to Ingeborg, who oversaw the distribution of its contents, and to all our generous donors.

Bookings: May and June were among our busiest months, with catering, accommodation and venue hire for workshops and celebrations. Everything ran smoothly.

Maintenance and repairs: the water pump and bore for the Admin House were completed, House 8 is nearly finished with a new kitchen sink, and the leaf hut conference area was repaired. Staff are planting flowers and preparing a vegetable garden.

SWIM FC is playing in the Hatanga Futsal League, with 3 wins and 4 losses so far. The women's ministry is learning sewing and studying strong women of the Bible such as Esther and Deborah. Children's teachers Martina Gegeu, Janet Light and Phillistus Wate completed training at the Evangelism School for Children and began a character-building phase. The youth ministry, led by John and Martina, is focusing on Christlike character.

Testimonies from Crossroads at Rove Correctional Centre: "I thought God couldn't love someone like me. But now I understand grace, and I want to live a new life with faith." Another student said, "I felt ashamed and lost. But through the Crossroad study, my eyes were opened. I'm no longer ashamed. I'm blessed and happy."

Praise points: God's grace on SWIM in the first half of the year; the Crossroads ministry, where 20 students were recognised for good behaviour; and a stable workforce, steady guests and the weekly ministries.

Prayer points: the leaders of the Solomon Islands, Prime Minister Jeremiah Manele and his government, and Governor General Sir David Tiva Kapu; SWIM's plans for the next six months; the new dormitory and 70 new students at Katova High School; and shipping materials for the Kwainafala water project.

A heartfelt thank you to the SWIM team, the board, base managers, LLT and all staff, and to our major supporters, the members of the CRC churches in Australia.
